title: Science and research
description: Academic words for describing experiments, evidence and findings, common in Reading passages and Listening Part 4.

words.definition: an idea that is suggested as an explanation and then tested
words.example: The researchers tested the hypothesis that noise affects bird song.

words.definition: based on observation or experiment rather than theory
words.example: There is little empirical evidence that the diet improves memory.

words.definition: the information discovered as the result of research
words.example: The findings suggest that children learn languages best through play.

words.definition: to organise and carry out an activity
words.example: The study was conducted over a period of ten years.

words.definition: a small group chosen to represent a larger population
words.example: The survey used a sample of 2,000 adults from across the country.

words.definition: a factor that can change in an experiment
words.example: Temperature was the only variable changed during the experiment.

words.definition: a connection between two things where one changes as the other does
words.example: Researchers found a strong correlation between sleep and exam results.

words.definition: something that happens or exists, especially something unusual (plural: phenomena)
words.example: The northern lights are a natural phenomenon caused by solar particles.

words.definition: an important new discovery in science
words.example: The discovery of penicillin was one of the greatest scientific breakthroughs of the century.

words.definition: the checking of research by other experts before it is published
words.example: All articles in the journal go through peer review.

words.definition: to repeat an experiment and get the same results
words.example: Other laboratories were unable to replicate the original results.

words.definition: not leading to a clear result or decision
words.example: The results of the trial were inconclusive, so further research is needed.

words.definition: a single example of a plant, animal or substance used for study
words.example: The museum holds over a million insect specimens.

words.definition: a room or building for scientific experiments
words.example: Results that work in the laboratory do not always work in real life.

words.definition: to examine something carefully to understand it
words.example: The team analysed soil samples from twenty different farms.

words.definition: the set of methods used in a particular piece of research
words.example: Critics questioned the methodology of the survey.

words.definition: to be one of the first to develop a new method or idea
words.example: She pioneered a new technique for repairing damaged nerves.

words.definition: money given for a particular purpose, such as research
words.example: Space exploration requires enormous amounts of funding.

words.definition: relating to beliefs about what is morally right
words.example: Animal testing raises serious ethical questions.

words.definition: relating to genes, the units passed from parents to children
words.example: Some diseases have a strong genetic component.

words.definition: to suggest an explanation for something
words.example: Scientists theorise that the dinosaurs were killed by an asteroid impact.

words.definition: the careful watching of something to learn about it
words.example: Years of observation revealed how the birds use tools.

words.definition: using new methods or ideas
words.example: The university is known for its innovative approach to cancer research.

words.definition: the first model of a new machine or product
words.example: Engineers tested a prototype of the solar-powered car in the desert.

words.definition: something that is different from what is normal or expected
words.example: The unusually warm winter was dismissed as an anomaly at first.

words.definition: to prove that something is true or correct
words.example: Further tests are required to validate the new vaccine.

words.definition: containing a mistake or weakness
words.example: The study was flawed because it included only male participants.

words.definition: a person who takes part in a study or activity
words.example: Participants were asked to keep a food diary for a month.

words.definition: a possible future effect or result
words.example: The research has important implications for how cities manage water.

words.definition: to say that something is not true or correct
words.example: Several experts dispute the claim that the drug is safe for children.
